newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait aromatics project decision by September.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait aromatics project decision by September.

text.p: Kuwait could make a final decision by September on a proposed aromatics project possibly worth up to $1.5 billion, industry sources said on Tuesday.
"I think the reviewing process could be completed by the end of the summer," an executive said.
Industry sources said a feasibility study for the project had been completed and is due to be reviewed by the state Petrochemical Industries Co's (PIC) board of directors.
PIC's parent, Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC), which runs the country's oil industry, will then review the study and PIC's recommendations.

Industrialists in Kuwait say an aromatics project is needed to start intermediate industries in the tiny Gulf state along with output from Equate Petrochemicals Co -- a $2 billion joint venture between PIC, Union Carbide Corp of the United States and the local Boubyan Petrochemical Co.
Equate is due to start production in August. Mechanical completion is scheduled for next month.

Last year Kuwait decided on a study of requirements after stopping joint venture talks on the aromatics project with Amoco Corp of the United States. PIC has already secured approval in principle for the private sector to take a stake in the project which could also be open to foreign partners.
Equate has an annual design production capacity of 650,000 tonnes of ethylene, 450,000 tonnes of polyethylene and 350,000 tonnes of ethylene glycol.

Kuwait, a co-founder of the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), controls about 10 percent of the world's oil reserves -- some 96.5 billion barrels. It currently produces about two million barrels per day.
PIC deputy chairman Abdullatif al-Haddad earlier told Reuters the company hoped to start production from the aromatics project by 1999 or 2000.
Using Kuwaiti naphtha as feedstock, the plant would produce materials such as benzene, xylene and paraxylene -- raw materials for textiles such as acrylic fibre.

Kuwait, which is keen to develop a refining and downstream network in Asia similar to its Europe operations, is a latecomer to the petrochemical industry in a region where Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states have spent billions of dollars over the past 15 years developing an advanced petrochemical industry.
